scope: Private research comparison of frozen small K1 against the one-wave candidate; not a fixed-v1 capsule benchmark, provider qualification or llama.cpp comparison.

baseline.label: small
baseline.description: Frozen small K1 shared-memory reduction: 32 threads for columns <= 32, otherwise 256.

candidate.label: onewave
candidate.description: One 32-thread block per row for all widths <= 1024; strided loads and reviewed width-32 value/index shuffle reduction. Requires warp size 32.

build.note: Compile phase used loader diagnostics and required no GPU lease; measured runs disabled diagnostics.

analysis.sample_units: microseconds per launch; each raw sample is HIP event elapsed time for a batch of 100 launches divided by 100
analysis.median_definition: Arithmetic mean of sorted samples at zero-based positions 9 and 10, separately for each provider, shape and trial.
analysis.ratio_definition: baseline_median_us / candidate_median_us; greater than 1 means a lower candidate median. Ratio of medians, not median of paired ratios.
verification: All compile and run receipt output byte counts and SHA-256 hashes verified against evidence files.
All three phases process-complete with return code 0 and no process failure; actual prefix evidence hashes match before/after and receipts report physical and semantic equality.
Both measured runs diagnostic=false, empty stderr, preflight passed, exclusive GPU lease held through phase receipt and released with matching phase SHA-256.
Executable identical across both trials, matching compile output; comparator and one-wave header match reviewed hashes, baseline variants header matches previous variants comparison compile.
Both providers passed CPU bit-value/index validation before and after timing in every case.
All 480 raw samples finite and positive; all 24 medians recomputed exactly and 12 baseline/candidate ratios calculated separately.
Shape, seed and input digest match across trials, and the original K1 comparison inputs.
Device identity, HIP versions and complete loader path list match across trials; loader path list matches prior K1 run.
limitations: Only six K=1 shapes and one deterministic distinct finite F32 input per shape on one gfx1151 device; no ties, NaNs or general-K qualification.
Two trials remain separate with no pooling, confidence intervals, statistical significance or broad workload claims.
The modest 32-column timing differences are descriptive observations; these two trials do not establish statistical significance. The wider-row regressions are preserved in full.
Provider measurement order alternates within each pair; shape order is fixed and system drift remains a possible influence.
HIP event batch timings include provider stream work and possible host enqueue gaps; they are not pure kernel latency. Input transfer, CPU validation, allocation and event creation are excluded.
The baseline here is our previous small function. No llama.cpp implementation, bitonic adapter, rocPRIM or separate control comparison was measured.

The upstream investigation reported by the coordinating reviewers found existing llama.cpp argmax already uses a warp/single-wave approach and greedy selection uses argmax. This artifact makes no argmax novelty or performance claim over llama.cpp. See docs/rocm-k1-upstream-overlap.md for the separately maintained source investigation.
Loaded paths are observations; metadata coverage remains unknown and vendor authenticity unverified.
External host/library hash snapshot checks reported by the root reviewer are not independently certified by this artifact; phase output files and loader path observations were independently checked.
Receipt hashes identify external evidence. Large prefix evidence files, executable and library contents are not embedded in this portable artifact.
observations: Against the frozen small baseline, one-wave median batch time per launch is about 3% lower at 32 columns in both trials.

At 256 columns, one-wave median time is about 18-19% higher; at 1024 columns it is about 1.95 times the small baseline time. These regressions rule out treating this candidate as a general winner for the six tested shapes.
These are descriptive per-case observations across two separate trials, not pooled estimates or a comparison with llama.cpp.
